research.research_themes: Data mining from biological and medical data Due to the amazing advances in molecular biology, various and huge amount of biomedical data are now available. Objective of this theme is discovery of novel knowledge of life through combination of various data and application of advanced data mining algorithms. Specific research topics include; prediction of protein function and structure, species identification from RNA sequence, discovery of genes distinctive in a gene expression dataset, etc. Text mining and intelligent search for biomedical literature In the field of life science, so many papers are published every year and it is impossible for a researcher to browse through all of them. Therefore, it is desired to search the papers intelligently and extract precious information and knowledge. Objective of this theme is, through the calculation of semantic similarity among words, enabling intelligent search of biomedical papers and automatic information extraction, rather than simple keyword matching and template matching, respectively.

research.research_themes: Data-Driven Model Mathematical models that represent the relationships among input variables, internal variables, and output variables of a system or process are founded on underlying physical laws and are fitted to observed real data to determine the parameters of the mathematical model. The approach of data-driven models involves extracting only the necessary data from a large dataset to determine parameters in a way that aligns with the intended use of the model, or directly extracting the necessary data without going through a mathematical model.Currently, we are working on data-driven modeling for the initial settings of the hot finishing rolling process to improve the precision of steel products. Data-Driven Predictive Control The utilization of mathematical models enables the estimation of unobservable state variables and the prediction of future states; however, the accuracy of these estimations and predictions is contingent upon the quality of the mathematical model. Model Predictive Control (MPC) leverages mathematical models to forecast future system behavior and determine appropriate control inputs. Conversely, our research is focused on developing a model-free predictive control method that predicts system behavior and determines appropriate control inputs using accumulated data, without relying on mathematical models. This approach is gaining attention as an effective method for controlling complex phenomena where model construction is challenging. Data-Driven Pole Placement Method Pole placement is a standard method to obtain a feedback controller when we are given desired closed loop pole locations as a control performance specification. To apply the pole placement technique, we need a mathematical model of the controlled system. The purpose of this study is to derive a pole placement method which does not require any models of the controlled system but its input/output data. Real-time optimization via extremum seeking control Extremum seeking control which is a sort of adaptive control enable us to find an optimal value of an uncertain cost function. In this study, we apply extremum seeking control to minimization of affect of nonlinearlity in control systems, maximization of power in electricity generation by renewable energy, and so on. research.research_themes: Support for the action and education for disaster mitigation The Noto Peninsula earthquake of 2007 made me think that I, as a geographer focusing on the region, a person with experience in geography education, and a researcher concerned with the fishing industry, might have applicable knowledge and opportunities for involvement, and I have started support work and research that will lead to an enhanced capacity for regional disaster prevention. More specifically, as a person involved in fisheries research, I deal with tsunamis, which can cause disasters along the coast.As a geography educator, I am involved in supporting and researching school and community disaster prevention related to earthquakes, floods, tsunamis, etc. Distribution and regions for fisheries and seafood, and study on learning and education for food and meal I focus on the distribution and consumption of fisheries products from a geographic viewpoint. From where and how are the marine products we are eating delivered? I am interested in the regional positioning and roles related to these activities, the links between regions and their expansion, the evaluation of the regions involved and food products, as well as indigenous food culture and dissemination and establishment of new diets. While focusing on the fishing industry and marine products, through geography and social studies education and daily diet, I also try to develop a curriculum about food and diet that is not limited to discipline and nutrition education. Creation, spread and enlightenment of illustration map I am interested in maps (depictions), which are one method/tool to look into a region as a person involved in geography and geography education. In particular, I intend to develop and disseminate “illustration maps” that do not require sophisticated techniques, that can be developed out of simple drawings representing individual interests in maps, and that do not limit their use to research and education. My intention is to promote interest in maps, geography, and the region among people who find map reading and drawing difficult, and who feel they have little connection with maps, by lowering the barrier and increasing options for coming into contact with maps.

research.research_themes: International political dynamics of cultural heritage making UNESCO's heritage programmes such as World Heritage and the Memory of the World promotes the heritage of outstanding universal value or world significance. In this regard, the inscription of the Nanjing Massacre documents into the "Memory of the World" Register in 2015 reflects an increasingly globalized concern over human rights issues in the post–Cold War era. At the same time, however, this decision has generated new controversy, because Japan (the perpetrator of the Nanjing Massacre) has expressed grave concerns over the inscription. research.research_themes: Developlment of High-Speed High-Efficient Technique of Nanoparticle/Nanomaterials Synthesis using Modulated Induction Thermal Plasmas Development of a High-Efficiency, High-Rate Production Method for Functional Nanoparticles Using Modulated Thermal Plasma: Nanoparticles refer to ultrafine particles with diameters below 100 nm. As particle size becomes extremely small, the surface area significantly increases, promoting surface reactions. Additionally, nanoparticles exhibit unique chemical, optical, electrical, and magnetic properties that are not observed in bulk materials. Due to these characteristics, nanoparticles are regarded as breakthrough materials in various industries, including materials, electronics, information and communication devices, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, housing, and foundational research in fields such as chemistry, physics, and biology. Notably, the demand for nanoparticles is steadily increasing in sectors like electronics, environmental science, energy, and healthcare. For the widespread societal application of nanoparticles, it is essential to industrialize nanoparticle synthesis. A key challenge in this regard is achieving large-scale production and commercialization of functional nanoparticles. In other words, technologies capable of producing nanoparticles in large quantities, at high speeds, with high precision, at low cost, selectively, and with high purity must be developed. The need for "nanoparticle mass production technologies" is so critical that it is regularly featured in the Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry’s (METI) "Technology Strategy Map." In this research, we aim to establish a method for the mass production of functional nanoparticles using a novel technique that we developed modulated inductively coupled thermal plasma (MITP) combined with precursor feed rate control. This approach allows for the rapid and large-scale synthesis of functional nanoparticles by modulating plasma energy and precisely controlling the input timing of precursor materials. Development of ultra high-speed non-equilibrium prcessings using PMITP Development of a High-Speed Nonequilibrium Process Using Modulated Inductively Coupled Thermal Plasma (MITP): High-power, high-enthalpy plasmas have recently emerged as a promising ultra-fast material processing source, thanks to advances in plasma technology. These plasmas possess extremely high enthalpy, and while they have historically been applied in fields like welding and thermal spraying to exploit their thermal energy, recent attention has shifted towards inductively coupled thermal plasmas (ICTP). These plasmas can generate high-enthalpy environments without electrodes, creating clean plasma spaces, which has made them increasingly relevant in materials science and plasma chemical processes. However, high-enthalpy plasmas come with significant challenges. Due to their extremely high gas temperatures, it is difficult to control the plasma without causing thermal damage to substrates or products. This has driven the need to establish new techniques that can control the gas temperature, flow velocity, and reactions in plasma, allowing for high-speed processes without sacrificing precision. To address these control challenges, we have developed several novel types of modulated inductively coupled thermal plasmas (MITP), such as: Pulse-Modulated Inductively Coupled Thermal Plasma (PMITP) Arbitrary Waveform Modulated Thermal Plasma (AMITP) Feedback-Controlled Inductively Coupled Thermal Plasma (FBC-MITP) These MITP systems allow intentional temporal fluctuations in high-enthalpy plasma on the order of tens of kW, enabling us to control the time-averaged values of heat flux, ion density, and radical density. Furthermore, by applying MITP for surface modification of materials, we have discovered a phenomenon where heat flux can be reduced, and radical species density can simultaneously be increased in the downstream region of the plasma. This finding is particularly significant because these two phenomena are typically contradictory under local thermal equilibrium theory, indicating the emergence of nonequilibrium effects arising from kinetic reactions within the plasma. Our findings demonstrate that these modulated plasmas create a temporally controlled environment governed by radical/ionized species kinetics, wherein the motion and reaction dynamics of heavy particles are precisely managed. One of the key advantages of this approach is the ability to maintain a thermal nonequilibrium state, where gas temperatures are kept at intermediate levels (3000-5000 K), while electron temperatures reach several electron volts (eV). This state allows for high radical densities by leveraging reaction nonequilibrium, all while avoiding the thermal damage that usually accompanies high-enthalpy plasmas. The objective of this research is to develop an advanced Highly Accurate Modulated Inductively Coupled Plasma (HTMC-ICP) and apply it to ultra-fast nonequilibrium processes for nanoparticle synthesis. By doing so, we aim to create a new generation of high-speed material processing technologies that harness the power of modulated plasma for precise and efficient production of nanomaterials. Development of Loop/Racetrack type of High-Pressure High-Temperature Modulated Plasmas for Large-Area High-Speed Processing Development of a New Loop/Planar-Type High-Pressure, High-Temperature Modulated Thermal Plasma Source for Large-Area Processing: Conventional inductively coupled thermal plasma (ICTP) devices typically use a cylindrical quartz vessel surrounded by a coil. A high-frequency current is applied to the coil, which sustains a cylindrical plasma inside the quartz tube. However, this cylindrical configuration poses limitations when applied to large-area thermal plasma processing. Specifically, scaling up such a torch for large-area applications requires an increase in the diameter of the cylindrical torch, which, in turn, demands significantly higher power to maintain the larger plasma volume. Moreover, due to the intrinsic Lorentz force, the plasma tends to contract radially, further complicating the ability to achieve large-area plasma processing. In response to these limitations, this research focuses on the development of a novel "planar-type inductively coupled thermal plasma device" that enables large-area processing by replacing the conventional cylindrical quartz tube with a planar quartz vessel. This device uses a planar quartz container sandwiched between air-core coils. When a high-frequency current is applied to the coils, an alternating magnetic field is induced perpendicular to the quartz vessel, which sustains a planar-shaped inductively coupled thermal plasma inside the vessel. To further enhance stability, we have developed a "loop-type inductively coupled thermal plasma torch," where the quartz vessel is shaped into a loop that follows the plasma flow. This loop-shaped configuration allows for highly stable maintenance of an argon plasma (Ar-ICTP) within the loop. By positioning a substrate downstream of the loop, we can maintain a long, linear thermal plasma that extends over the substrate, making it highly suitable for large-area treatments. Our research not only aims to further improve the uniformity of these planar and loop-type plasma devices but also explores their applications in ultra-high temperature annealing processes, as well as in large-area surface modification and thin-film deposition. By introducing reactive molecular gases into the plasma, we anticipate additional benefits in terms of chemical reactions at the substrate surface, which could enable more precise control over film formation and surface treatments. In summary, this study presents a breakthrough in large-area thermal plasma processing, overcoming the limitations of traditional cylindrical torches through the development of planar and loop-type plasma sources. These new designs enable efficient, stable, and large-scale surface processing, with potential applications in advanced material processing techniques such as high-temperature annealing and thin-film deposition. Study on High Current Arc Interruption Phenomena for Development of Green/Carbon-Neutral Society Innovative Research on High-Current Arc Interruption Phenomena: In recent advanced information society, the backbone of economic and technological growth is undeniably the reliable and high-quality supply of large-scale electrical energy. During high-voltage transmission, short-circuit currents caused by system faults can reach nearly 80 kA. Power circuit breakers bear the critical responsibility of interrupting these high currents swiftly and securely. The technology to break such high fault currents is not only the core of high-reliability power transmission but also one of the most technically challenging areas of electrical engineering. As economic development accelerates, particularly in countries like China, ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission systems are being introduced, including 1000 kV AC and ±800 kV DC systems. These require further advancements in high-current interruption technologies. In Japan, UHV technology development began in the 1990s, but most of the innovations were extensions of the existing 500 kV technology. With the large-scale integration of renewable energy being explored, including the use of DC grids, the need for advanced DC circuit breakers is becoming increasingly important, especially in Europe and China, where development of these systems is already underway. At the same time, from the perspective of global warming, environmental impact reduction has become a critical challenge for high-current interruption technologies. Presently, the predominant technology used in power circuit breakers involves SF6 gas (sulfur hexafluoride), which is highly effective at arc quenching. However, SF6 is an extremely potent greenhouse gas, with a global warming potential (GWP) 23,900 times that of CO2 over a 100-year period. SF6 has been identified as a gas requiring reduction under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and subsequent COP (Conference of Parties) agreements. This has led to an urgent demand for the development of compact, energy-efficient arc chambers that minimize SF6 usage, as well as for the creation of alternative arc-quenching media and new interruption methods. This research focuses on a dual approach, combining high-precision experiments and advanced numerical simulations to unravel the fundamental mechanisms of high-current arc interruption phenomena. Through this interdisciplinary collaboration, we aim to elucidate the underlying physical principles that govern arc plasma behavior during current interruption, laying the groundwork for next-generation power systems. The goal is to develop "compact and highly efficient arc interruption technologies" that not only meet the needs of today's power systems but also pave the way for future systems that are both environmentally friendly and technically advanced. Specifically, we aim to address the following key challenges: Understanding arc plasma dynamics: By using cutting-edge diagnostic tools and high-precision simulations, we aim to capture the complex interplay of thermal, electrical, and fluid dynamics in the arc plasma during high-current interruptions. Development of novel arc-quenching methods: Building on the insights gained from our fundamental research, we are exploring new arc quenching techniques that use either reduced amounts of SF6 or alternative, more environmentally benign gases. Application to DC and UHV systems: With the shift toward DC transmission and UHV grids, particularly for renewable energy integration, we aim to extend these technologies to DC circuit breakers, where interruption is even more challenging due to the lack of current zero-crossings. This comprehensive approach will not only clarify the core principles of arc interruption but also contribute directly to the development of more sustainable and efficient power circuit breakers, ensuring the reliability and environmental responsibility of future power grids.

research.research_themes: An attempt to apply the value distribution theory to number theory by means of difference. Trying to develop a 'difference' method to evaluate an equidistribution in view of R. Nevanlinna's value distribution theory but independent of those of meromorphic functions, we hope to understand a variety know such results in number theory in this context and to extend some of them by taking account of the difference of elements in the distribution. Difference can catch up with differential? For the purpose to reduce a certain computational complexity, we observe a possibility to replace a role of differential operator by that of difference operator without any approximation and examine to what degree it can be made initially for analytic functions. Then we are going to apply those results in fields of computer technology after rehashing them for piecewise-linear and continuous functions that permit max-plus series expansions. Tropical value distribution theory and applications We have extended the Nevanlinna theory on meromorphic functions on the complex plane to the theory on piecewize linear and continuous functions on the real line for the purpose to apply it to the study on ultra-discrete equations. Study on Value Distribution of Meromorphic or algebroid Functions and holomorphic curves The research to refine those estimates in the Nevanlinna-Cartan theory on meromorphic or algebroid Functions and holomorphic curves in a complex projective space and to apply them to the related subjects. Application of the value distribution theory to the study on complex differential and functional eguations Application of the value distribution theory to the study on complex differential and functional eguations Study on differential or difference equations appearing in many areas and value distribution of meromorphic functions or holomorphic curves We apply the value distribution theory of meromorphic functions or holomorphic curves for the study of possible transcendental meromorphic solutions and their systems to differential, (q-)difference or ultradiscrete equations appearing in many areas. Our main subject is to transplant the theory into the corresponding field as in its most suitable formulations.

research.research_themes: Medical application of robot technology Images are a type of information that can be conveniently measured. By extracting human movement from these images and analyzing them, we are developing methods of disease estimation, object manipulation procedure detection, and emotion detection etc., which are capable of application in various fields such as medical welfare, engineering, and psychology. Adhesion Forces Reduction by Oscillation and Its Application to Micro Manipulation In the micro region, for scale effect, the force (attracting force) proportional to the area and length of van der Waals attraction, surface tension, and electrostatic force become dominant compared to the force proportional to the force of gravity and inertia. These attracting forces create an adhesion force between the target object and tool. To cope with this adhesion force, we are proposing a method of mitigating adhesion force through vibration. By minutely vibrating the end-effector and contacting it (bringing it near to) with the physical object on the table (foundation), the adhesion force between the end-effector and physical object will become small compared to the force between the table (foundation) and physical object. By applying this method, we can manipulate objects in the same way as manipulation of the micro region. Based on this method, we are developing methods of automatically conducting various macro manipulation. Object grasping and manipulation by robotic hand (../file/image_004072.png)

research.research_themes: Development of a computed simulation program to train clinical judgement for fall prevention The aim of this study is to develop computed simulation program to train clinical judgement for fall prevention. A collaborative approach for the prevention of falls in stroke patients Preventing falls in stroke patients during rehabilitation cannot be successful without effective collaboration. The aim of this study was to qualitatively evaluate a collaborative approach for fall prevention. The collaborative approach involved sharing values and attitudes (i.e., consciousness), education, and approaches, followed by integration and clarification of one’s own roles. We tested two teams comprising nurses (NS), physiotherapists (PT) and occupational therapists (OT) through simulation with stroke patients during rehabilitation. Descriptive data were collected via interview, and analyses used employing a framework approach. Answers to interview questions revealed that sharing consciousness, education, and approaches had the power to change, involving in recognition of “Sharing consciousness having the power to change towards a positive direction”, “Being able to understand other professions’ perspectives and ideas”, “Taking advantage of documentation provided by nurses”, and “Nurses documentation being a shared tool”. “Compensate phenomena among roles” was shown through integration and clarification of one’s own roles. These data suggested that a collaborative approach was effective in a qualitative analysis, quantitative analyses are planned for a future study. Development of a fall prevention program adapted to the individual risks of elderly persons in facilities The aim of this study was to develop a fall-prevention program adapted to the individual risks of elderly patients in a long-term care facility by increasing the caregiving skills and motivation of staff members through mutual action research. The program, developed through the synthesis of seven evidence-based practice studies, consisted of staff education, identification of problems related to fall prevention in the facility by the use of focus group interview, assessment of individual risks, implementation of care adapted to the risks, consultation about fall-related problems, and modification of care in case of falls. The fall-prevention program was shown to be effective, especially in reducing injuries. The fall rate per 1,000 residential days was reduced from 7.6 to 5.0 in the intervention ward, while it went from 4.8 to 4.3 in the control ward. The percentage of injured persons in the intervention ward was significantly reduced from 22.6% during the 6 months before the intervention period to 9.7% during the 6-month intervention period, and the number of injuries was reduced from 13 to 3. No one was harmed by the program. The process went from expectation and anxiety regarding an unpredictable process to feeling of achievement through role conflicts. Empowerment was considered a driving force. The change agents for staff members were the response of patients and family members to satisfactory care, and the recognition of the need for cooperation with other medical staff members. On the other hand, the change agent for the fall prevention team members was recognition of staff members who could identify individual risks and had potential care skills. In conclusion, the fall-prevention program was shown to be acceptable for use among elderly individuals in a long-term care facility by increasing the caregiving skills and motivation of staff members. Fall prevention for the elderly in a long-term care institution: Development of an exercise program based on EBN Our aim was to develop an exercise program for fall prevention, based on evidence-based nursing (EBN), to not only increase muscle strength in the lower extremities, balance, and mobility, but also to decrease fear of falling and to increase self-efficacy for fall prevention in the elderly in a long-term care institution. We developed an exercise program which consisted of a warm-up, static stretching exercise, muscle strengthening in the lower extremities, balance training (toe training and proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation), and a cool-down, based on EBN. The study design was a clinical trial. We developed a program through two trials. In the first trial, the 30 elderly participants who agreed to our study were divided into an intervention group of 16 people and a control group of 14 people. The length of the program was three months, and we measured muscle strength, balance, mobility, fear of falling, self-efficacy for fall, and the number of falls to evaluate the effectiveness of the program. As a result, the intervention group showed increased balance and mobility and a decreased number of falls, although muscle strength and self-efficacy for fall did not increase and arm strength decreased significantly. No training-related medical problems occurred. We modified the program to increase muscle strength in the lower extremities, to increase or maintain arm strength and self-efficacy for fall. In the second trial, 40 elderly participants were divided into an intervention group of 21 people and a control group of 19 people. The results showed a maintaining of arm strength and an increase of self-efficacy for fall but no increase of muscle strength in the lower extremities. In conclusion, an exercise program for fall prevention in the elderly in a long-term institution may be useful. Life management platform using social big-data for elderly home assistance The purpose of this study is to develop the life management platform. This platform uses the remote sensing technologies and the analyzing technologies. The remote sensing technologies are a method of collecting behaviors of elderly and home environments by monitoring public utilities and using the variety of sensors. The analyzing technologies are a method of predicting assist information by collecting data. research.keywords: Factor XIII-A, CNS regeneration, transglutaminase, Yamanaka factors, HSF1, wound healing, zebrafish，optic nerve, retina
research.research_themes: Study of CNS regeneration Mammalian central nerves, once injured, become irreversibly damaged and the damage leads to functional loss. In contrast, neuraxon regeneration is possible with the central nerves of fish. For example, when optic nerves are severed in goldfish, neurites re-elongate at the severed end in about a week, regenerated neuraxons reach the arget optic tecta in about a month, and subsequently, after synaptic reorganization, optic functions themselves are fully recovered in 5-6 months. Characteristically in fish, neuron deaths are suppressed first to maintain life after neuraxon injury, and then manifestation of molecules is induced to newly elongate neurites. By explaining this regeneration mechanism, I explore the possibility of central neuraxon regeneration in mammals. research.research_themes: Patterns of Difficulty Experienced by Nurses Caring for Elderly Patients with Dementia in Medical Facilities The purpose of this study was to describe and clarify nurses' experience of difficulties with institutionalized elderly patients with dementia in medical facilities. This study was a qualitative study using grounded theory guided data collection and analysis. Twenty-seven registered nurses (RN) who care for elderly with dementia in medical facilities were interviewed. Finally, a core category emerged following the refinement of categories and diagrams. Dimensions of Accepting patients and their situation was the core category and four categories were identified : An encounter with demented patients, necessity to watch, the tension of the routine work, and conflict between families and nurses. Antecedent conditions were an encounter with demented patients and conflict between families and nurses.

research.research_themes: Histopathological changes of joint components by joint contracture. Joint contracture is a part of disuse syndrome induced by reduced joint movement caused by regional immobilization, bedrest, etc., and accounts for a large portion of clinical caseloads in physical therapy. However, consensus is yet to be reached on the pathology of joint components affected by joint contracture, despite the publication of various reports on the subject. We developed a joint contracture model by using various methods to immobilize the knee joints of rat hindlimbs, and have been histopathologically observing changes in joint components (e.g. joint cartilage, joint capsule, synovium, fat tissue), clarifying the effects of physical therapy treatment, and examining more effective treatment approaches. research.research_themes: Genetic analysis and expression studiesin congenital cogulation factor deficiencies and coagulation inhibitor deficiencies I conduct genetic analysis of individuals with congenital coagulation factor deficiencies and coagulation inhibitor deficiencies, and their families, to identify the mutation sites. I have analyzed coagulation factor deficiencies in terms of prothrombin, factors VII, X, XI, XII, and prekallikrein, as well as coagulation inhibitor deficiencies in terms of protein C, protein S(PS), antithrombin, and have continuously demonstrated new mutation sites that had not been reported internationally. Further, I generate abnormal molecules with a recombinant DNA procedure and conduct their functional analysis. PS deficiency is important also as a cause of habitual abortion, and the demand for its genetic analysis will likely increase. Mechanism of thrombosis in arteriovascular disease With regard to arteriosclerosis and thrombosis, I examine hyperlipidemia and thrombotic tendency with molecular markers and manifestation of monocytic coagulation−fibrinolytic factors upon lipoprotein stimulus. Recently, I have been conducting research on the effect of an antihypercholesterolemia, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin), on coagulation−fibrinolytic system as a pleiotropic effect, and have clarified that statin down-regulate monocytic tissue factors in vascular endothelial cells and the manifestation of a coagulation−fibrinolytic factor PAI-1, while down-regulate the manifestation of anticaking factor TFPI, thereby demonstrating the potential for anti-thrombogenicity effect.
